2197: These conveyors are designed to convey materials between different elevation levels. They are equipped with an adjustment system that can be manual or electric, allowing the height to be changed as needed. They are widely used in processes where materials have to be moved between different floors or platforms, such as vertical production lines or storage systems.
2199: Ideal for conveying materials in a straight line on a horizontal plane, these conveyors are essential in assembly lines, distribution centers and other environments where continuous, linear movement of materials is needed. They ensure the constant movement of products between different stages of the production process, maintaining operating efficiency.
2201: Made up of segments that can be adjusted to different angles, these conveyors are perfect for layouts that require flexibility in movement. They allow changes of direction or incline, which makes them ideal for industrial plants with complex layouts or layouts that change frequently, making it easier to convey materials along non-linear paths.
2203: Inclined conveyors are designed to move materials along a fixed angle, without the need for constant adjustment. They are often used in processes that require constant lifting or lowering of products, such as transferring materials to different levels of a production line or loading and unloading at different levels.
2205: Some industrial operations have specific requirements and need custom-built conveyors. Special conveyors are designed to meet these unique demands, whether through specific materials, custom dimensions or unique features that meet the customer's needs exactly, ensuring maximum efficiency and fit with the process.
2207: Roller conveyors are sturdier and ideal for conveying heavy loads. They use rollers arranged in series to support and convey the materials. Depending on the application, these conveyors can be configured in different ways:
2209: This type of conveyor operates without a drive, allowing materials to move by gravity or be pushed by hand. They are ideal for environments where flow control is not critical, such as storage areas or assembly lines where products need to be moved by hand over short distances.
2211: Equipped with powered rollers, these conveyors offer precise control over the movement of heavy materials. They are particularly useful in automated processes, where conveying speed and direction need to be regulated to ensure continuous, efficient flow, as in high-volume production lines.
2213: Designed to change the direction in which materials are conveyed, curved conveyors are essential in industrial facilities where space is limited or the layout requires changes of direction. They allow smooth, continuous movement of materials around curves, without compromising conveying speed or stability.
2215: Flexible or extendable conveyors are highly adaptable, designed to fit different layouts and distances as needed. They can be extended, retracted and adjusted in shape and length, which makes them ideal for dynamic work environments, such as logistics centers and factories that need conveying solutions that can be quickly set up for different tasks. These conveyors are especially useful where space is limited and flexibility in moving materials is essential to maintain operating efficiency.

2219: The base that supports the belt and the other components.
2221: Responsible for moving the belt and controlling the speed.

2225: A belt conveyor works by moving the belt through a drive and pulley system. The material is placed on the belt, which carries it along the defined path. The speed and direction of the belt can be adjusted as needed to meet operating demands.
2227: Efficiency: belt conveyors allow continuous, automated conveying of materials, drastically reducing the time needed to move items from one point to another. This results in a significant optimization of the workflow, allowing production to keep a constant pace without interruptions. In addition, the automation these systems provide reduces the need for manual intervention, freeing the team to focus on higher-value tasks.
2228: Versatility: belt conveyors are highly adaptable and can be customized to convey a wide range of materials, from light, delicate products to heavy, bulky loads. This versatility allows them to be used in different sectors, such as the food, pharmaceutical, mining and logistics industries. In addition, conveyors can be designed to operate in adverse environments, such as high temperatures, corrosive environments or areas with high dust levels, ensuring they meet the specific needs of any operation.
2229: Safety: by reducing the need for manual handling of materials, belt conveyors significantly minimize the risk of work accidents, such as repetitive strain injuries or falling heavy loads. Safety systems, such as automatic stop sensors and protective barriers, can be integrated into the conveyors to prevent incidents, ensuring a safer work environment that complies with regulations.
2231: Preventive maintenance is crucial for belt conveyors to work well. Some essential steps include:
2232: Regular inspection: carry out periodic inspections to check belt tension, the alignment and condition of the rollers, and the state of the bearings. Small faults detected early can be corrected before they cause bigger problems, avoiding unexpected production stoppages.
2233: Lubrication: keeping all moving parts of the conveyor well lubricated is crucial to avoid premature wear and ensure that the components run smoothly. Choosing the right lubricant, depending on the environment and the materials conveyed, can extend the equipment's service life.
2234: Cleaning: regular removal of dirt, dust and debris that build up on the conveyors and components is vital to avoid blockages and operating failures. Cleaning also helps maintain hygienic conditions in industries such as food, where contamination can be a risk.
2236: Continuous monitoring: implementing a continuous monitoring system to follow the conveyor's performance in real time allows early detection of any anomaly. This makes it easier to make adjustments before small problems turn into major failures.
2237: Employee training: training the team to carry out daily visual inspections and identify signs of wear or malfunction can prevent serious failures and extend the equipment's service life. Well-trained employees can also carry out basic maintenance, reducing dependence on outside services.
2238: Component replacement: establish a schedule for replacing critical components, such as belts and rollers, before they reach the end of their service life. This ensures the conveyor keeps performing efficiently and avoids unscheduled stoppages.
